description: Declaration, amendment, cancellation and goods-arrival payloads must pass HMRC XSD schema validation before CDS processing begins.
hmrc_reference: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design | v2.30 | Section 2.2 Technical Validation Carried out on all Declarations
source_title: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design
page_or_section: Section 2.2 Technical Validation Carried out on all Declarations
acceptance_criteria: Payload conforms to the HMRC-published XSD for the API and version in use.
No datatype, element-order or invalid-element schema errors are returned.
HTTP 400 is not returned by the API gateway.
verification_steps: Validate the payload against the relevant HMRC XSD.
Submit the payload with the correct Accept header.
Confirm that no BAD_REQUEST or xml_validation_error response is returned.

description: Payload content must not trigger the HMRC web application firewall regular-expression rules.
hmrc_reference: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design | v2.30 | Section 2.2 Web Application Firewall (WAF) Validation
source_title: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design
acceptance_criteria: Free-text fields do not contain blocked character combinations or keyword patterns.
The API does not return PAYLOAD_FORBIDDEN or Internal server error at WAF stage.
verification_steps: Populate the message with production-like free text.
Check the text against HMRC WAF examples and recommendations.
Submit the payload and confirm that WAF does not reject it.

description: CDS does not accept batch declaration submission; declarations must be submitted individually.
hmrc_reference: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design | v2.30 | Section 2 Scope for Declaration Management
source_title: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design
acceptance_criteria: Each API call contains one declaration message only.
No batch wrapper or multi-declaration payload is sent.
verification_steps: Review the integration request builder.
Confirm one declaration per API request.
Submit and verify normal asynchronous processing.

description: Local Reference Number (LRN / submitterReference / DE 2/5) must be unique against accepted and registered declarations and cannot be reused within 48 hours.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS12003
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: DE 2/5 is unique for the trader among accepted and registered declarations.
A rejected declaration's LRN may be reused; an accepted or registered one may not be reused within 48 hours.
verification_steps: Submit a declaration with a new LRN.
Resubmit the same LRN within 48 hours for the same trader.
Confirm HMRC returns CDS12003 for the duplicate submission.

description: DE 1/9 Total Number of Items must equal the number of goods items declared.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS11003
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: DE 1/9 matches the count of goods-item structures in the payload.
No extra or missing goods-item nodes exist relative to DE 1/9.
verification_steps: Build a declaration with a known item count.
Set DE 1/9 to the correct number and submit.
Repeat with a mismatched value to confirm CDS11003.

description: All goods items on a declaration must derive the same procedure category.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS11005
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: Every item's DE 1/10 and DE 1/2 combination derives the same declaration category.
No mixed-category declaration is submitted.
verification_steps: Derive the category for every item using the HMRC derivation matrix.
Confirm all items resolve to one category before submission.
Submit a mixed-category declaration to confirm CDS11005 is returned.

description: Net mass must be lower than gross mass.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS11006
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: Where both masses are declared, net mass is less than gross mass for the same scope.
verification_steps: Populate gross mass and net mass for the same item or header.
Check that net mass is lower than gross mass.
Submit a failing case to confirm CDS11006.

description: A goods-arrival notification must follow a pre-lodged declaration in a permissible state.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS12014
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: A pre-lodged declaration exists for the reference used by the goods-arrival message.
The referenced declaration is in a state that permits arrival.
verification_steps: Submit a pre-lodged declaration.
Submit a goods-arrival message for that declaration.
Repeat with a non-pre-lodged or invalid-state reference to confirm CDS12014 or CDS12015.

description: Goods-arrival notifications must be submitted within 30 days of the pre-lodged declaration.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS12031 / CDS12046
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: Arrival is submitted within the 30-day window measured from the original declaration receipt date.
verification_steps: Record the receipt date of the pre-lodged declaration.
Submit arrival within 30 days and confirm acceptance.
Submit after 30 days to confirm CDS12031 or CDS12046.

description: A new amendment or cancellation request cannot be submitted while a previous request is still awaiting response.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS12036
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: Only one in-flight amendment or cancellation request exists per declaration lifecycle point.
verification_steps: Submit an amendment or cancellation request.
Before a response arrives, submit another request.
Confirm HMRC returns CDS12036.

description: The submission channel of an amendment must match the original declaration channel.
hmrc_reference: CDS Error Codes | 11-03-2026 issue | CDS12034
source_title: CDS Error Codes
acceptance_criteria: The amendment uses the same submission channel as the original declaration.
verification_steps: Record the channel used for the original declaration.
Submit the amendment through the same channel.
Submit through a different channel to confirm CDS12034.

description: The secure file-upload service accepts at most 10 files, each up to 10 MB, and only jpeg, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, or png formats.
hmrc_reference: CDS Secure File Upload UI User Guide | v0.44 | Section 3.1.5 File Upload
source_title: CDS Secure File Upload UI User Guide
acceptance_criteria: No more than 10 files are uploaded in one submission set.
Each file is 10 MB or smaller.
Each file extension is one of jpeg, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, png.
verification_steps: Prepare a set of supporting-document files.
Confirm file count, size, and extension before upload.
Upload the files and verify a document reference code is returned for each accepted file.

description: Avoid %, ?, &, tabs, and other special characters in secure-file-upload filenames because the service may behave unexpectedly.
hmrc_reference: CDS Secure File Upload UI User Guide | v0.44 | Section 3.1.5 File Upload
source_title: CDS Secure File Upload UI User Guide
error_code: BAD_REQUEST | HTTP 403 PAYLOAD_FORBIDDEN | Unexpected file-read failure
acceptance_criteria: Filename characters are HTTP-safe and do not contain %, ?, &, tabs, or special characters flagged by HMRC.
verification_steps: Inspect each filename before upload.
Rename files containing reserved or special characters.
Upload and confirm successful document-reference issuance.

description: Avoid semicolons, equals signs, slash characters in goods descriptions, and SQL-keyword patterns in free text because these combinations are known WAF triggers.
hmrc_reference: WAF Trigger Examples | v0.4 | General Advice tab (GA1-GA4)
source_title: WAF Trigger Examples
acceptance_criteria: Free-text fields do not contain ';', '=', SQL-keyword strings, or '/' in goodsDescription where HMRC has flagged them as trigger patterns.
Known trigger examples are removed or rewritten before submission.
verification_steps: Review all free-text fields in the XML payload.
Compare them against the WAF Trigger Examples workbook.
Replace or rewrite flagged strings before submission.

description: MUCR values must match HMRC's published CDS MUCR formats, contain no more than one hyphen, and MRNs must not be submitted as export movements.
hmrc_reference: CDS Guidance for Software Developers - MUCR Format | Baselined | Sections 2 and 4 Appendix
source_title: CDS Guidance for Software Developers - MUCR Format
error_code: MUCR reference is invalid | DMSREJ / ILE NAK
acceptance_criteria: MUCR length is 35 characters or fewer.
MUCR matches one HMRC-published CDS format.
No MRN is used in place of a MUCR on export movement messaging.
verification_steps: Generate MUCRs from one of the HMRC-published format families.
Check length and hyphen count before movement submission.
Submit a failing format to confirm rejection behaviour in exports inventory linking.

description: Authorisation references declared in DE 2/3 and DE 3/39 must match HMRC-published CDS authorisation formats for the declared authorisation type.
hmrc_reference: CDS Guidance for Software Developers - Validation of Authorisations | v1.9 | Authorisations Table
source_title: CDS Guidance for Software Developers - Validation of Authorisations
acceptance_criteria: The declared authorisation or licence reference matches the HMRC format for its type.
The reference belongs to the declared party and is valid for the scenario.
verification_steps: Identify the authorisation type being declared.
Validate the reference format against HMRC's authorisation guidance.
Submit a declaration with an invalid or mismatched reference to confirm the relevant CDS1200x error.

description: Where a tariff measure requires a document, CDS returns CDS40045 if the required document is missing; where a measure condition or range is not met, CDS returns CDS40066.
hmrc_reference: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design | v2.30 | Section 6.3 Tariff Measure Validation Failures
source_title: CDS Declaration Submission Service Design
acceptance_criteria: All document-based measure conditions are declared on the affected commodity lines.
All value, ratio, or other measure conditions are satisfied for the affected commodity lines.
verification_steps: Retrieve the applicable tariff measures for the commodity/origin combination.
Populate all required documents and measure-condition data.
Submit a negative test without the condition to confirm CDS40045 or CDS40066.

description: The Accept header must target the TDR API version for each subscribed CDS API, including Customs Declarations API v1.0 in TDR.
hmrc_reference: Developer set up | Customs Declarations End-to-End Service Guide | Web page | API versioning
source_title: Developer set up | Customs Declarations End-to-End Service Guide
acceptance_criteria: The request Accept header matches the TDR API version subscribed for that environment.
The application is allow-listed and subscribed to that API version.
verification_steps: Inspect the outbound request headers.
Confirm the application subscription for the TDR version.
Submit a request with an incorrect Accept header to confirm HTTP 406 behaviour.

description: TDR should be used for realistic, day-in-the-life declaration proving with real account data, not for performance or exploratory technical testing.
hmrc_reference: CDS RunBook | v4.3 | Slide 17 Guidance / Slide 2 Connecting to TDR
source_title: CDS RunBook
page_or_section: Slide 17 Guidance / Slide 2 Connecting to TDR
acceptance_criteria: TDR test scenarios use realistic declarant data and declaration journeys.
The proving pack excludes performance, load, or exploratory protocol testing in TDR.
verification_steps: Review the planned TDR scenarios with the declarant.
Confirm the data set is realistic and authorised for TDR use.
Run technical experimentation and load tests only in the appropriate non-TDR environment.

description: Submission planning must account for HMRC's published service-availability notices, planned maintenance windows, and queued-processing warnings.
hmrc_reference: Customs Declaration Service: service availability and issues | Web page | Current and historical update entries
source_title: Customs Declaration Service: service availability and issues
acceptance_criteria: Submission windows are checked against the HMRC service-availability page before go-live or dress-rehearsal runs.
Exports needing Permission to Progress are not first submitted during a published queueing window.
verification_steps: Check the latest HMRC service-availability page before executing the test window.
Record any planned maintenance or outage affecting exports or imports.
Adjust the run schedule to avoid queueing or blackout periods.
